To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the driver's intent is best inferred using the generic, curvature-based parameterization and the Bayesian network classifier with dynamic Bayesian inference; b) the driver's future trajectory can be accurately predicted using the same parameterization and a simple, non-parametric approach to predict the future velocity of the vehicle; and c) the driver's maneuver is best inferred using a generic model parameterized with observations at an individual location, while the driver's trajectory is best inferred using observations at a generic location.

the proposed driver intent inference approach is able to predict the turn and stop maneuvers with an accuracy of 95% and 98.7%, respectively, and that the driver model is able to predict future trajectories with a root-mean-square error of 2.2 m.

the proposed approach is able to predict driver behavior with an accuracy of 80-90% for a generic model and of 95-98% for an individualized model, depending on whether the preceding vehicle is stopped, moving or turning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an approach to infer a driver's intent based on the vehicle's speed profile, even when the vehicle is being driven in a platoon with a preceding car.
the problem of inferring driver intent at urban intersections in the presence of preceding vehicles by using the vehicle's velocity profile.

the following questions: (1) What are the best parameterization choices for a simple, real time capable driver model for urban intersections? (2) How well can a simple driver model predict the future trajectory of a vehicle at an urban intersection?

velocity-based driver intent inference in the presence of preceding vehicles can be performed with a high level of accuracy using a simple, parametric model of car-following and driver behavior.

, in contrast to previous approaches, the driver model can predict a driver's intent even in the presence of a following vehicle, which is a prerequisite for the deployment of advanced driver assistance systems at urban intersections.
